fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Strange, Wanda, and America as Gnostic Figures", "body": "Chance opened his breakdown by saying he did not accept the Gnostic myth as literal history and used it only as a lens for the film. He cast Doctor Strange as the divine savior in the mold of Pythagoras, Christ, Hermes or Thoth, with Sagittarius as his sign. He read Wanda as Sophia and the demiurge at once, and said that swapping the letters W and M turned Wanda into Manda, which he took to mean gnosis. America became a young Eve, and Chance tied the mother and daughter struggle to a thesis on the dragon mother."}, {"title": "Title Codes and Letter Swaps", "body": "Gabe, handed the introduction, noted that the film arrived in the month of Mother's Day and that the initials of its title could be rearranged to spell mom. Chance argued later that mad is the root of madre, that dam is the mother, and that damned is an anagram of maddened, so blaming Eve meant blaming the mother. One of the hosts reported that strange and shortage matched across twenty two gematria ciphers. One of the hosts connected the hero's cape to the word escape, and another noticed the doctor's rival was named West."}, {"title": "Ciborium, Tower Card, and Perseus", "body": "For the opening scene, one of the hosts read the floating light as the point above the Tree of Life. Gabe explained the ciborium, a four posted canopy that shelters an inner sanctum, and said the film was steeped in them. The hosts counted sixteen points in the stained glass and tied that to the Tower card, then read the chase across broken columns as Perseus rescuing Andromeda at the spring equinox. Gordy outlined the three gods behind the Book of Vishanti, and one of the hosts tied that book to Pegasus as a page."}, {"title": "Fantasia and the Brocken Spectre", "body": "When a monster attacked the city, Gabe noticed the horn music came from the Night on Bald Mountain sequence in Fantasia. He followed it to Mount Brocken in Germany, where he said an early live Olympic broadcast was made. He described the Brocken spectre, in which the sun throws a climber's shadow onto the clouds as a giant, and compared it to Plato's cave and to broadcasting fear to a crowd below. The others reacted with surprise, and one of the hosts suggested the topic deserved a show of its own."}, {"title": "Trauma, Dreams, and the Medusa Mother", "body": "Gordy answered Chance's question about dreaming by suggesting the film's dream selves were a way of integrating different versions of oneself, said Strange's many variants were all just him, and said real wizard duels happen in the astral realm. One of the hosts read Wanda as Medusa and as a cephalopod, a word meaning head foot, so a mind walker who attacks through clouds of ink. Gordy added that an octopus keeps much of its brain in its arms. Gordy also read Strange's watch as the symbol of his trauma."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The InnerVersal mystics of Marvel return to integrate the shadow of the Dark Mother Goddess & the Man of Light, with an incredibly deep analysis of Dr. Strange and the Multiverse of Madness. Rife with Gnostic Christian allegory and a psychologically shattered-mirror perspective on the All-Mother, this film may just be the wildest thing we've covered yet.
